hook_text: A shoe factory makes 1 245 pairs a day for 236 days. How many pairs is that in a year?
clip_script: Pinetown shoe factory: 1 245 pairs a day, 236 days a year. Big sum? Break up 236: 200, 30 and 6. Times 6: 7 470. Times 30: 37 350. Times 200: 249 000. Add them: 293 820 pairs! In columns it is one row per digit. Tens row? Start with one zero. Hundreds row? Two zeros. Forget them and your answer shrinks. Check with an estimate: about 1 200 times 240 is 288 000. Close! Three rows to the answer.
visual_style: A column multiplication building row by row, placeholder zeros dropping in like bricks, with a stack of shoe boxes growing.
mood: Industrious and steady, like a factory line.
pacing: One row at a time with a beat for each placeholder zero, then the add-up and estimate.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find 3 408 times 125.
